title: HateXplain three-class probe readout
question: M1.40 把 HateXplain 的 offensive 归为 0；三分类下 R12/rescan 相对 f32 的差异是否改变？

dataset.name: HateXplain
dataset.note: Same cleaned rows and embeddings as M1.40; only the label head changes.

modeling.c_selection: f32 only, 5-fold StratifiedKFold on fit, 3-class accuracy; f32 and quantized arm share C

primary.verdict: descriptive only; no confirmed/rejected candidate verdict

secondary: binary-equivalent accuracy (hatespeech vs rest) is not recomputed here

H1_offensive_confound.statement: If offensive is a hard-negative class that the binary mapping hides, the three-class arm-f32 difference may differ from the binary result, especially on offensive recall.

H2_no_candidate_rescue.statement: A three-class exploratory readout cannot upgrade R12/rescan; it can only motivate a later preregistered three-class test.

independence_and_boundaries.seeds: 5 seeds share test texts; not independent.
independence_and_boundaries.label_mapping: three-class labels are the corpus native majority labels; no soft labels / annotator disagreement in M1.43.
independence_and_boundaries.candidate: R12 and rescan remain rejected in the binary primary; this is a mechanism/readout check.

prereg_commit_policy: Committed before running model-score or accuracy computation.
